Where's that user that said linux virus scans can never make sense for any user under any circumstance?

This article makes my point. Linux is not a set it and forget it environment and whatever someone does to monitor their security shouldn't be mocked. (Not something I do on linux but someone else wanted to take an interest in it and recieved a lot of backlash).

Articles like this are frustrating. Like the zillions of ransomware articles, the writers have done their homework and have a huge amount of information about the malware and what it does. They usually completely skip telling the reader how the malware might get on the machine or network.

Was it through a user casually visiting a common news site? I worry about passive drive-by infection but have controls in place,

Or was it through someone who has been trained to not click on attachments from emails they never expected to receive because they don't know the sender? OK, I'm worried, but we have controls in place for these users, too. Plus all monolithic OS installs will always be risky (not beating up on Redmond but Windows seems to be the one common denominator in the ransomware epidemic.)

Or was it installed by hand by an insider to intentionally compromise the network? Now this would have my attention. But they never say.

So a rootkit exists but I cannot quantify the risk because I can't determine anything about how it gets installed beyond some proof of concept in a lab.
